description: Evaluation dataset for IOC extraction from IBM banking trojan article

test_cases.content: The malware communicates with its C2 server at hxxps://dlxfreights.site/uadmin/gate.php to exfiltrate stolen credentials.
Multiple C2 endpoints were identified including hxxps://facturacionmx.autos/api, hxxps://facturamexico2023.com/api, and hxxps://russk22.icu for command and control operations.
The campaign also uses hxxps://jogjaempatroda.com as an additional C2 infrastructure.
The malware connects to IP address 192.168.1.100 and 10.0.0.5 for data exfiltration.
Network traffic analysis revealed connections to 203.0.113.42 and IPv6 address 2001:db8::1.
The malicious file has MD5 hash 5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592.
Multiple samples were identified with MD5 hashes: 098f6bcd4621d373cade4e832627b4f6 and d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e.
Analysis revealed SHA256: 2c26b46b68ffc68ff99b453c1d30413413422d706483bfa0f98a5e886266e7ae for the payload.
The malicious Chrome extension ID is abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz123456.

The banking trojan campaign uses multiple infrastructure components. The primary C2 server is located at hxxps://dlxfreights.site/uadmin/gate.php, with backup servers at hxxps://facturacionmx.autos/api and hxxps://russk22.icu. The malware also connects to IP addresses 192.168.1.100 and 203.0.113.42 for data exfiltration.
This is a generic security blog post about malware trends without any specific indicators of compromise.
The article discusses general cybersecurity best practices and threat landscape overview.
